title: Thermostat-style Autoscale Targeter with Safety Curtains and Contracted Minimums
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a thermostat-style autoscaler that targets contracted throughput while minimizing cost and ensuring safety envelopes for Dedicated fleets. This ticket specifies target metrics, scaling algorithms, and multi-layer safety limits. It will be the canonical policy implementation for scale-up/scale-down decisions for committed capacity and burst lanes.

Context: Current autoscalers focus on percentile targets and headroom credits. Customers with reserved Dedicated capacity ask for hard throughput guarantees (contracted rps/token throughput) plus predictable unit economics. We need an autoscale controller that: (1) directly maps to a throughput contract, (2) integrates cost feedback so bursts don't blow budgets, and (3) enforces strict safety curtains to prevent cascading scale churn across tenants and zones.

Core deliverables:
- A targeter component that converts observed signals (p50/p95 latency, per-tenant RPS, token/sec, queue length, KV cache hit affinity) into an actionable throughput target expressed in GPU-shares and reserved slots.
- A thermostat control loop combining smoothed percentile estimation, derivative damping, and quantized step sizing to avoid oscillation.
- Safety curtains: min-contracted floor, emergency floor, per-tenant bleed limits, and global quota gates.
- Cost-awareness: integrate recent-cost-per-token and a configurable cost budget to reduce non-essential scale during expensive epochs.
- Operational knobs: manual override, canary scaling mode, cooldown windows, and graceful drain policies for eviction.

Out of scope: model compilation optimizations, kernel-level batching changes, and UI work (Console tickets will follow for dashboarding).
acceptance_criteria: Targeter produces a deterministic GPU-slot recommendation given a set of synthetic workloads and a contract definition
Controller scales up/down without more than 10% overshoot for 95% of test traces using the lab harness
Safety curtains prevent tenant-triggered multi-zone cascading scale events in stress tests
Cost feedback reduces non-critical burst scaling when projected hourly spend exceeds configurable threshold
Integrations: GitHub PR merged for runtime code, integration tests in CI, and a Confluence design doc linked
comments: 2026-02-04 - Asha: Initial design sketch added to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/thermostat-autoscale-targeter). Proposed three layers: signal processing, thermostat controller, and safety gates.

2026-02-12 - Diego: PoC of percentile smoother in dev cluster shows reduced jitter but slow recovery on sudden demand spikes. Noted that derivative damping parameter needs tuning (link to simulation results: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scale-sim/pull/17).
2026-02-20 - SRE review (Rina Gupta): Recommend emergency floor be a separate fast-path informed by warm lanes to avoid cold-start churn. Added dependency on ENG-612345 for warmup lanes integration.

2026-02-28 - PM review (Evan Moore): Product asks to expose contracted-minimum as API field and add telemetry labels for billing reconciliation. Added acceptance criterion for deterministic mapping to GPU-slot recommendation.

2026-03-03 - Diego: Implemented quantized stepper and cooldown windows in runtime branch. Opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234. Early tests show reduction in oscillation but occasional underprovision on sudden 4x bursts.

2026-03-08 - Performance: Ran 50 synthetic traces; controller meets overshoot target on 48/50. Two failing traces correlated with high KV-miss rates and inter-zone network tail latency. Added plan to incorporate KV-affinity weighting.

2026-03-10 - Asha: Design updated to add cost-feedback loop that consults the hourly burn estimator and disables non-essential burst lanes when projected spend exceeds tenant budget. Updated Confluence doc and added runtime feature flag.
2026-03-10 - Next: finalize PR, add integration tests for multi-tenant safety curtains, and schedule canary rollout to 2 dedicated pools after QA signoff.
